Session storage content in the user's browser

regulations.name: GDPR
regulations.reason: EU/EEA jurisdiction. Triggering facts: the product accepts free-text input that a user may populate with personal data, and requests are processed on servers whose region is not declared in the brief. Missing facts: whether the service is offered to EU data subjects, the hosting region, and the retention period of request logs. Required action: confirm territorial scope and hosting region, then document the lawful basis and a retention period for logs.

regulations.name: CCPA / CPRA
regulations.reason: California, United States. Triggering facts: the brief targets software teams without excluding US users. Missing facts: annual revenue, number of California consumers processed, and whether any personal information is sold or shared. Required action: verify the applicability thresholds for the current calendar year before launch.

regulations.name: Open-source license compliance
regulations.reason: Applies wherever the software is distributed. Triggering facts: the product ships third-party dependencies and generates artifacts that embed dependency references. Required action: keep a locked dependency manifest, verify each license against the allowed list in CI, and preserve required attribution notices.

regulations.name: AI provider terms and data processing
regulations.reason: Contractual, applies wherever the provider is used. Triggering facts: user-submitted text is sent to a third-party model provider for processing. Required action: sign or accept the provider's data processing terms, disable training on submitted content where the provider offers that control, and disclose the sub-processor in the privacy notice.

regulations.name: Cookie and tracking consent (ePrivacy)
regulations.reason: EU/EEA, only where non-essential storage is used. Triggering facts: the product stores state in the browser's session storage for functional purposes only, which is generally exempt. Required action: keep browser storage strictly functional and document that no analytics or advertising identifiers are set; add a consent mechanism if that changes.

regulations.name: COPPA
regulations.reason: United States, children under 13. Confirmed facts that exclude the rule: the service is directed at professional software teams, is not child-directed, and the brief declares no features or content aimed at minors, so no actual knowledge of under-13 users arises from the described design.

regulations.name: PCI DSS
regulations.reason: Contractual security standard for cardholder data environments. Confirmed facts that exclude the rule: the described product collects no payment data and operates no cardholder-data systems. This changes the moment a paid tier is introduced.

regulations.name: HIPAA
regulations.reason: United States, covered entities and business associates. Confirmed facts that exclude the rule: the product is not offered to health care providers, plans or clearinghouses, and processes no protected health information.
